subject: Runtime instrumentation & platform comparison — decision criteria
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Muro <caroline.muro@pritech.com>
Cc: Derek Walsh <derek.walsh@pritech.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Runtime instrumentation & platform comparison — decision criteria

Hi Caroline — great to meet yesterday. Thanks for walking us through PriTech's inference use cases and the team constraints (single-region, 99th percentile latency requirement at 120ms, and the compliance checklist). I promised a short recap + proposed next steps focused on the operational tooling comparisons you asked for.

Quick recap (from our call):
- Primary decision drivers: latency SLOs, per-token cost at 1M+ monthly tokens, and visibility into per-request tracing (end-to-end request IDs across proxies + model runtime).
- Current pain: hyperscaler endpoints provide metrics but sampling makes debug cycles slow; no easy KV cache hit/miss telemetry; cost spikes during batchy traffic.
- Stakeholders: Caroline (platform lead), Derek (infra), SREs (engineering).

Suggested next steps (proposed):
1) Share instrumentation checklist (attached) and ask your SREs to run a single low-effort probe against a sandboxed endpoint (we can provide short curl + trace headers).
2) Run a 48-hour parallel run: PriTech traffic replay to Redwood demo cluster vs your hyperscaler endpoint. Focus metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, per-request token cost, KV cache hit rate, and availability under spike.
3) Tech deep-dive with Ben (cc'd) on the trace propagation and sampling model — 30 mins.

Deliverables we'll provide: instrumentation checklist, an abridged Redwood vs hyperscaler feature matrix (attached), and a test harness for request replays.

If that plan looks good I'll schedule the replay window and the Ben deep-dive next week.

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: instrumentation-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.pdf (summary)
From: Caroline Muro <caroline.muro@pritech.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Derek Walsh <derek.walsh@pritech.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime instrumentation & platform comparison — decision criteria

Thanks Sergio — that recap is spot on. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- Derek wants to understand how Redwood surfaces KV cache behavior per request (we currently only have aggregate hit-rate counters). Can you call out exact trace spans/attributes we should expect?
- On cost: we run two main workloads (interactive chat + nightly batch embed job). For the replay, can we prioritize the chat traffic (interactive) and sample the batch job 10%?

We can run the instrumentation checklist by the SREs today. I'll have Derek loop back with availability for the 30m tech deep-dive.

Also — curious if Redwood supports async trace ingestion to our Splunk instance or if you recommend forwarding via a collector. Derek — please add any constraints.

Best,
Caroline
VP Platform Engineering, PriTech Inc.
From: Derek Walsh <derek.walsh@pritech.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Caroline Muro <caroline.muro@pritech.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime instrumentation & platform comparison — decision criteria

Quick note from infra: we prefer forwarding traces via an internal OpenTelemetry collector (Splunk OTEL), so async ingestion is preferred over direct push. Also we have a limit on outgoing egress to non-approved endpoints — for the parallel run we'll need a private endpoint or a short-lived IP allowlist.

Derek
Sr. Infra Engineer, PriTech
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Derek Walsh <derek.walsh@pritech.com>, Caroline Muro <caroline.muro@pritech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime instrumentation & platform comparison — decision criteria

Thanks Derek — good to know. Short answers:
- Trace model: Redwood exports full request traces with span attributes for request_id, route, model_variant, batch_size, kv_cache_hit (true/false), kv_cache_key_len, and tokens_generated. We can emit OTLP compatible spans to your collector; we also support S3-batched trace export if you prefer pull.
- For the parallel run: we can spin a private demo endpoint in your region and provide a short-lived IP allowlist + signed cert. That keeps egress minimal.

Action items I'm picking up:
- Ben: please confirm the sampling/default retention on traces we propose for the 48h run and whether we can surface KV cache hits as a per-request boolean in trace UI (this impacts their debugging speed).
- Marissa: can you prepare a pared-down dashboard layout (p50/p95/p99, token-cost per route, KV cache hit rate over time, and a trace-link column) we can hand off to PriTech SREs?

I'll schedule the deep-dive while we wait for the SREs to run the checklist. Proposed windows: Wed 13 Apr 16:00-16:30 PT or Thu 14 Apr 09:00-09:30 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks,
Sergio
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Caroline Muro <caroline.muro@pritech.com>, Derek Walsh <derek.walsh@pritech.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 14:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime instrumentation & platform comparison — decision criteria

On Tue, Apr 13, 2027 at 10:15 AM Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Action items I'm picking up:
> - Ben: please confirm the sampling/default retention on traces we propose for the 48h run and whether we can surface KV cache hits as a per-request boolean in trace UI (this impacts their debugging speed).

Short answers: yes and yes. Details below.

Sampling & retention for the 48h run:
- Default sampling: 100% for request spans from the demo endpoint for the 48h window (we can raise/lower by route).
- Retention: full-span retention for 7 days in the demo account; metadata/aggregates retained 30 days. We can export raw spans to S3 for longer-term retention if PriTech wants.

KV cache visibility:
- We will add a boolean span attribute "kv_cache_hit" and an integer "kv_cache_key_len". The demo UI will show a per-request column and allow filtering for cache-miss traces. That should address Derek's debugging speed concern.

Marissa — tagging you to draft the dashboard; aim for a one-page SRE view (latency percentiles, cost per route, cache hit/miss rate, and a trace-link column). I'll attach the sample dashboard and the short run playbook to the HubSpot deal after this thread.

Ben
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-demo-trace-sample.json (small), demo-run-playbook.md (internal)
